_note: Toolchains, tools and named chains taken from the project owner's own repositories and starred list. Every entry was verified with `git ls-remote` on 2026-11-17; anything that did not answer was left out. A toolchain is a real compiler a build can select. A tool is a utility the builder or a workflow shells out to.

toolchains.name: AOSP + Clang12 + SDCLang kernel toolkit

toolchains.name: AOSP external/llvm

toolchains.name: Clang 12 NDK toolchain
toolchains.note: Clang 12 for aarch64. Good default for 5.10: modern enough for current Android, old enough not to trip old kernel code.

toolchains.name: ARM GCC 4.8 (arm-eabi)
toolchains.note: 32-bit ARM GCC from the pre-GKI era. Needed for 3.x/4.x trees whose asm a modern clang refuses.

toolchains.name: GIMPLE GCC obfuscator
toolchains.note: GIMPLE-level obfuscation for C/C++/Go. Carries an incomplete 4.1.0 tree, so only its `sub` pass is safe.

toolchains.name: GOAT obfuscation augmentation
toolchains.note: GCC obfuscation augmentation tools -- the plugins, not the compiler. Pairs with gimple-obfuscator.

toolchains.name: Prebuilt GNU ARM toolchain

toolchains.name: Qualcomm CPU LLVM toolchain
toolchains.note: Qualcomm's LLVM for CPU-side user space (the sibling of SDCLang for DSP/hexagon work).

toolchains.name: Snapdragon LLVM (SDCLang)
toolchains.note: Qualcomm's optimised LLVM. Better code on sm* SoCs, and it does build kernels -- but kernel patches must match its version.

toolchains.name: LLVM prebuilt distribution
toolchains.note: Stock LLVM prebuilt, several versions. The unmodified baseline every obfuscator fork is diffed against.

toolchains.name: LLVM unofficial prebuild (wide API)
toolchains.note: Unofficial LLVM build with a broader exported API surface -- needed when a pass plugin expects internals a release build strips.

toolchains.name: Portable C++ cross toolchain
toolchains.note: Portable C++ cross compiler for user space and host tools. Not a kernel toolchain.

toolchains.name: Hallucina (LLVM obfuscation)
toolchains.note: LLVM-based obfuscation aimed at confusing automated analysers rather than humans.

toolchains.name: Hikari for LLVM 12
toolchains.note: Naville's HikariObfuscator for LLVM 12; the fork that pairs with the Clang-12 era NDKs.

toolchains.name: Hikari for LLVM 19-20
toolchains.note: Hikari obfuscator for LLVM 19/20 -- stronger anti-debug and indirect-branch passes than plain OLLVM.

toolchains.name: Hikarust (out-of-tree pass plugin)
toolchains.note: Out-of-tree, dynamically loadable Hikari pass -- no need to rebuild LLVM to use it.

toolchains.name: Kagura (anti-tamper passes)
toolchains.note: LLVM pass plugin for native code obfuscation, CFG integrity and anti-tamper.

toolchains.name: Modern LLVM obfuscator
toolchains.note: Second modern OLLVM-family fork; differing pass defaults, useful as a cross-check.

toolchains.name: Modern OLLVM (LLVM 22)
toolchains.note: OLLVM rebased onto LLVM 22. Newest OLLVM here, so it pairs with modern NDK user space.

toolchains.name: NDK toolchains with LLVM obfuscator

toolchains.name: O-MVLL (pass-based)
toolchains.note: Pass-based obfuscator that attaches to a stock clang build, so no LLVM fork is required.

toolchains.name: Obfuscator NDK 23
toolchains.note: Android Obfuscator NDK 23. Prepackaged, Windows-oriented.

toolchains.name: Obfuscator-LLVM (optimised)
toolchains.note: A slightly optimised OLLVM fork -- the same passes with less compile-time cost.

toolchains.name: Obfuscator-LLVM (plugin pass)
toolchains.note: OLLVM shipped as a loadable pass plugin. Has to be loaded into a matching LLVM, not used standalone.

toolchains.name: Obscura (Hikari/O-MVLL successor)
toolchains.note: Aim is to replace Hikari and O-MVLL, which have stalled; newer and less battle-tested.

toolchains.name: OLLVM packaged for the NDK
toolchains.note: Easily build and package Obfuscator-LLVM into an Android NDK. The container route to the same passes.

toolchains.name: Pluto (LLVM 12.0.1)
toolchains.note: Obfuscator based on LLVM 12.0.1 with control-flow flattening and bogus-flow passes.

toolchains.name: Polaris (LLVM)
toolchains.note: LLVM-based obfuscator protecting software at several levels of intensity.

toolchains.name: Zyrox (compile-time LLVM plugin)
toolchains.note: LLVM-based compile-time obfuscation plugin. Smallest scope of the obfuscator families.

toolchains.name: obfus.h (compile-time macros)
toolchains.note: Macro header for compile-time C obfuscation with tcc on x86. Not an Android chain.

toolchains.name: Obfusk8 (header-only C++17)
toolchains.note: Header-only C++17 obfuscation library. Nothing to install; drop it in and include it.

toolchains.name: smudgeC (source-to-source)
toolchains.note: Source-to-source C obfuscator. Runs before the compiler, so it works with any chain underneath.

toolchains.name: Khaos (inter-procedural)
toolchains.note: Inter-procedural obfuscation from the Khaos paper, with a hidden branch published here for study.

toolchains.name: M/o/Vfuscator
toolchains.note: The single-instruction C compiler -- everything becomes MOV. A curiosity, x86 user space only.

toolchains.name: x86-64 asm obfuscation
toolchains.note: Deliberately inefficient x86-64 assembly obfuscation. Demonstration scale.

toolchains.name: Rust LLVM plugin host
toolchains.note: Rust bindings for writing LLVM passes. Useful for a userspace pass, and the honest reason it is catalogued: it shows a Rust toolchain is present, not that it can build a kernel.

toolchains.name: Hikarust
toolchains.note: Hikari LLVM rewritten with a Rust-facing build. A C++/LLVM toolchain with Rust tooling around it, which is why it is listed here and not as a kernel-safe chain.

toolchains.name: Go protobuf (AOSP external)
toolchains.note: Go host tool from the AOSP tree. Host stage only: it generates code for the build, it does not compile anything that ships.

toolchains.name: Go cmp (AOSP external)
toolchains.note: Dependency of the Go host tools above. Catalogued separately because its branch tracks a different Android release, so pinning one does not pin the other.

toolchains.name: Kotlin compiler
toolchains.note: AOSP's in-tree Kotlin compiler, on the pie-era branch. The system stage is where it applies: Kotlin becomes Java bytecode, which is dexed, never compiled to machine code.

toolchains.name: jdiff
toolchains.note: API-diff tool for the framework. Host stage: it compares two builds' public API, which is how a system image change gets caught before it ships.

toolchains.name: absl-py (AOSP external)
toolchains.note: Python support library used by kernel and platform build scripts. It is a library, not a compiler: it belongs to whichever stage's scripts import it.

toolchains.name: clang-tools static binaries
toolchains.note: Wrapper that fetches static clang tools; the repo itself is Python, which is why it sits in this family rather than with the compilers it downloads.

toolchains.name: Brutal busybox
toolchains.note: The shell the initramfs and recovery actually run. Static, so the fused root does not need a matching libc for it.

toolchains.name: Kali NetHunter busybox
toolchains.note: NetHunter's applet set. A different busybox from the one above: different applets, different version, and scripts written for one can fail on the other.

toolchains.name: Keystone assembler
toolchains.note: Assembler framework for kernel entry stubs and for writing test sequences against vendor code.

toolchains.name: dotnet-obfuscation (third party)

tools.name: KPatch-Live (kpatch livepatching, x86_64)
tools.use: build a livepatch that patches the running kernel without a reboot
tools.builder_use: x86_64 counterpart to KPatch-Next-Module. kpatch_1 supplies kpatch-build, which compiles a source diff into a livepatch .ko; the KPatch-Live module (kpatch-live/ in this repo) ships it and loads it at boot through CONFIG_LIVEPATCH.
tools.notes: KPatch-Next-Module is arm64-only (its customize.sh aborts otherwise, and its inline-hook code is arm64 assembly); upstream kpatch is x86-64 and s390 with no arm64 support. So these are counterparts, not a port of one to the other, and neither can run on the other's arch. kpatch also works from a source diff and replaces function bodies, where a .kpm hooks functions at runtime. The module refuses to load a patch whose recorded kernel does not match uname -r, because loading a mismatched livepatch rewrites live kernel text with wrong offsets. Applies to x86_64 only: nothing here covers AR-NUKI-genevn.

tools.name: Tigress (source-level obfuscator)
tools.use: source-to-source obfuscation of user-space C before compilation
tools.builder_use: Stage target for the licensed Tigress tree you already have locally. It is not a git dependency -- it is an unpacked, licence-bearing directory -- so the workflow links ~/toolchains/tigress instead of cloning anything, and warns loudly if that path is missing rather than silently substituting some other copy.
tools.notes: User-space only, deliberately: Tigress transforms C source, and the substitution and flattening passes both wreck kernel code that depends on exact control flow and inline asm. The kernel-stage obfuscator refusal in workflow-gen.ts already blocks this if it is selected for a kernel role. Got here by send-toolchains.sh, not by a git fetch.

chains._note: Named compiler chains, one pick per build. Each chain names the toolchain used for the kernel and for user space separately, because they are not the same requirement: kernel code must be built by a compiler the tree was tested against and must never go through an obfuscator; user space is far more forgiving. `obfuscator: true` means the builder refuses the chain when the target is a kernel.

stock-aarch64.label: Stock aarch64 kernel
stock-aarch64.note: Safe default for the mobile kernel: Clang 12, no obfuscation.

stock-x86_64.label: Stock x86_64
stock-x86_64.note: Default for the desktop edition and kernel-zenith.

stock-baseline-llvm.label: Stock LLVM baseline
stock-baseline-llvm.note: The untouched upstream LLVM build. Use it to prove a bug is not the toolchain's fault before blaming an obfuscator fork.

llvm-wide-api.label: LLVM wide-API
llvm-wide-api.note: Unofficial LLVM with a broader exported API, for out-of-tree pass plugins that need internals a release build strips.

aosp-gcc-arm.label: AOSP GCC (32-bit ARM)
aosp-gcc-arm.note: Pre-GKI 32-bit trees that modern clang cannot assemble.

gnu-arm.label: GNU ARM toolchain
gnu-arm.note: Plain GNU cross toolchain, the non-AOSP route for arm and aarch64.

kernel-tools-wrapper.label: AOSP+Clang12+SDCLang kernel toolkit
kernel-tools-wrapper.note: Uses the bundled kernel wrapper set; user space stays on plain AOSP clang.

qualcomm-tuned.label: Qualcomm-tuned
qualcomm-tuned.note: Qualcomm's own LLVM on both sides. Best code on sm* SoCs, but kernel patches must match its version.

qualcomm-kernel-safe.label: Qualcomm user space, stock kernel
qualcomm-kernel-safe.note: Same benefit as qualcomm-tuned without betting the kernel on SDCLang.

cpp-hosts.label: Portable C++ (host tools)
cpp-hosts.note: For building host tools and user-space helpers rather than a device image.

ollvm-plugin.label: OLLVM pass plugin
ollvm-plugin.note: OLLVM as a loadable pass: the LLVM underneath must match the plugin's version.

ollvm-optimised.label: OLLVM optimised
ollvm-optimised.note: Same OLLVM passes with less compile-time cost.

ollvm-22.label: OLLVM on LLVM 22
ollvm-22.note: Newest OLLVM; pairs with modern NDK user space.

ollvm-x.label: OLLVM (xollvm)
ollvm-x.note: Second modern OLLVM-family fork; different pass defaults, useful as a cross-check.

ollvm-ndk-docker.label: OLLVM via NDK
ollvm-ndk-docker.note: The packaged NDK route to the same passes.

ndk-obfuscated.label: Obfuscated NDK toolchain
ndk-obfuscated.note: Obfuscator baked into the NDK driver, so nothing extra to load.

hikari-19.label: Hikari (LLVM 19-20)
hikari-19.note: Hikari on modern LLVM: anti-debug and indirect-branch passes beyond plain OLLVM.

hikari-12.label: Hikari (LLVM 12)
hikari-12.note: The Hikari fork that matches the Clang-12 era NDKs.

hikari-plugin.label: Hikari (out-of-tree plugin)
hikari-plugin.note: Loadable Hikari passes: no LLVM rebuild required.

polaris.label: Polaris
polaris.note: Selectable intensity levels; heavier passes cost markedly more compile time.

obscura.label: Obscura
obscura.note: Intended successor to Hikari and O-MVLL. Newer, so less battle-tested.

omvll.label: O-MVLL (pass-based)
omvll.note: Attaches to a stock clang build, so no LLVM fork is required.

kagura-chain.label: Kagura (anti-tamper)
kagura-chain.note: CFG integrity and anti-tamper alongside obfuscation.

hallucina-chain.label: Hallucina
hallucina-chain.note: Aimed at automated analysers rather than human readers.

gimple.label: GIMPLE obfuscated user space
gimple.note: GCC route. Only the `sub` pass is safe; the 4.1.0 tree is incomplete.

goat-gimple.label: GOAT + GIMPLE
goat-gimple.note: Augmentation plugins on top of the GIMPLE pass. Same `sub`-only rule.

khaos.label: Khaos (inter-procedural)
khaos.note: Inter-procedural obfuscation; x86_64 user space only.

movfuscator-chain.label: M/o/Vfuscator
movfuscator-chain.note: Everything becomes MOV. A curiosity; x86 user space, not a shipping option.

smudge-chain.label: smudgeC (source-level)
smudge-chain.note: Rewrites C before any compiler runs, so the chain underneath is free.

obfusk8-chain.label: Obfusk8 (header-only)
obfusk8-chain.note: Include-only C++17 obfuscation; nothing to install.

obfush-chain.label: obfus.h (tcc macros)
obfush-chain.note: Compile-time macros with tcc on x86. Not an Android chain.

categories.label: Rust
categories.note: Rust compiles into the system image and into the bootloader; a kernel-side Rust module needs the kernel's own rustc, so this is not offered for the kernel stage.

categories.label: Go
categories.note: Go is a host-tool language here: the build's own helpers are written in it. It is never a kernel compiler.

categories.label: Java / Kotlin (JVM)
categories.note: The Android framework is Java, and Kotlin is Java bytecode. These tools compile and dex the system image; they cannot produce kernel code.

categories.label: .NET / C#
categories.note: Relevant to userspace tooling and to obfuscating it. Nothing in a NUKI kernel or an Android system image is .NET, so it is a host/userspace-only family.

categories.label: Python
categories.note: Build scripts, firmware extraction and packaging. Present in every stage as glue, never as a compiler for shipped code.

categories.label: Shell (ash / bash / busybox)
categories.note: The initramfs and recovery run on shell. The choice of shell implementation is a real decision: busybox ash is not bash, and a script that uses bashisms fails at boot, not at build time.

categories.label: Assembly / disassembly
categories.note: Assemblers and disassemblers for the kernel's entry code and for reading vendor blobs.

stages.label: Bootloader / ESP
stages.romPart: U-Boot, edk2, the UEFI ESP and its stub
stages.why: Boot code runs before any runtime exists. A miscompile is an unbootable machine, so this stage takes a plain compiler only.

stages.label: Host tools
stages.why: Runs on the runner, not the device. Version freedom is highest here.

stages.label: Kernel image
stages.romPart: the NUKI kernel, its modules, ZeroMount and SUSFS hooks
stages.why: Must match the compiler the tree was tested against. Obfuscation here does not fail to compile, it boot-loops.

stages.label: System / user space
stages.romPart: bionic, the framework, apps, the fused Linux user space
stages.why: The only stage where obfuscation is safe: a fault kills one process, not the kernel.

stages.label: Recovery
stages.why: Recovery bundles a kernel, so it inherits the kernel rule.

stages.label: Vendor / DSP
stages.romPart: camera, audio, modem and Hexagon DSP blobs and HALs
stages.why: Vendor LLVM (SDCLang, cpullvm) is tuned for these cores and is the normal choice.
